description_en: The site is located in the hamlet of Hāṭa Gāũ, situated on the northern bank of the Ḍoṭī Gāḍ river, directly to the north of the larger settlement of Buḍhī Ghaṭāl.The site is mainly constituted of two structures built with reused medieval elements dating from the 14th-15th century. Inside the eastern structure (001), architectural elements from aśikharatemple are found laying on the ground. Inside the western structure are fiveśivaliṅgas. None of theśivaliṅgasare oriented to the north, hence indicating that they are all in secondary position and that there must have been at least fiveśikharatemples in the vicinity. There is also a stone Nandi in the western corner. In front of the western structure are two stone lion statues (003) and (004) and another one of Nandi (005).Hāṭa Gāũ is found in a valley directly south of Ajayamerukoṭa. Ajayamerukoṭa is rich in monuments that were mostly erected during the 14th and 15th centuries. According to D. P. Ojha, Ajayamerukoṭa was a local capital of the Khasiya kings from Jumla, (i.e. the Khaśa Malla emperors, 12th-14th century) (Ojha 1989: 54). From the mid-14th century, Ajayamerukoṭa seems to have taken greater importance as a capital of the Doti kingdom, especially under the reign of king Niraya Pāla (r. c. 1362-1383 CE). Indeed, it is around Niraya Pāla's time that Doti emerged as an entity independant from the Khaśa Malla empire. This political and economical rise is demonstrated in the numerous monuments erected between the second half of the 14th century and throughout the 15th century. Given the proximity of Hāṭa Gāũ with the site of Bhagavatī Asigrāma (DDL0040) and with Ajayamerukoṭa and the style of the architectural remains found there, it is likely that the artefacts at the site are dating from the same period, i.e. circa 14th-15th century.
references: REFERENCES Ojha, D. P. 1988. Doti Kṣetrako Itihās tathā Saṃnskrīti . Kathmandu: Sudur Paścimāncal Sāmājik Sevā tathā Anusandhān Samiti.
